cap_confirmation: Explicitly re-checked here because this is the Mt. Chimney milestone battle. The driver reported level_cap 36 and the resolved levels were Torkoal offset 0 -> L34, Mawile +2 -> L36, Sandygast +4 -> L38, Numel +5 -> L39. Every one equals 36 + offset - 2 (Medium), so the Mt. Chimney cap of 36 is the correct window for this battle and no --cap adjustment was needed. The same held for every battle in my block (97-108).

attempts.note: 4-0 without losing a Pokemon. Incineroar's Fake Out denied the one full-HP Eruption on turn one, and after that Excadrill's Ground STAB - which sun does not touch - was 2x into three of the four members while Togekiss stood beside it immune to Earthquake.

strategy_checks.check: Torkoal supplies actual sun via Drought
strategy_checks.evidence: Turn-0 state already read weather B_WEATHER_SUN_NORMAL before any command, 'The sunlight is strong.' printed each turn, and it faded on schedule after T5 - correctly outliving Torkoal itself, which died on T3.

strategy_checks.check: Torkoal's Eruption is the payoff of the sun
strategy_checks.evidence: Torkoal selected MOVE_ERUPTION on T1 and was flinched by Fake Out; it selected Eruption again on T3 and was KOed by Rock Slide first. A full-HP sun-boosted Eruption is the strongest thing this team can do and it never resolved. The AI picked the right move both times - this is a fragility problem, not a decision problem.

strategy_checks.check: Numel's Simple doubles Flame Charge's Speed boost
strategy_checks.evidence: Numel had three decision turns (T4, T5, T6) and chose Earth Power, Protect and Earth Power. Flame Charge was never selected, so the Simple interaction - the reason the dossier gave Numel Speed investment and an Eviolite instead of 'another Amnesia loop' - did not appear. Simple was live on the stat block.

strategy_checks.check: Mawile trades Swords Dance for Knock Off
strategy_checks.evidence: T4 Mawile's selected move was MOVE_KNOCK_OFF aimed at Excadrill. Swords Dance is correctly absent from the set and no setup move was chosen. Intimidate also fired on entry, dropping both of my attackers.

strategy_checks.check: Sandygast's Water Compaction is reactive and does NOT grant Water immunity
strategy_checks.evidence: I deliberately used no Water move in this battle - sun halves Water damage, so Mega Gyarados was benched and Earthquake led instead. The ability therefore never had a trigger. Recording the reasoning because the dossier flags this as a point of confusion: it is a +2 Defense on being hit, not an immunity, and that is correctly what the set says.

strategy_checks.check: Sandygast uses Shore Up recovery behind Eviolite
strategy_checks.evidence: Sandygast used Protect on T1 and Earth Power on T2 and T3. Its Eviolite was removed by Knock Off on T2 (Dark is 2x into Ghost, taking it from 125 to 10 in one hit) and it died on T3 before recovery was worth anything.

strategy_checks.check: Ground pressure is unaffected by the weather (my counterplay)
strategy_checks.evidence: Earthquake is 2x into Torkoal, Numel and Mawile and sun does nothing to it. Excadrill threw it from T4 onward with a Flying-type partner and it took Mawile (critical) and Numel. This is the whole answer to a sun team whose members are three-quarters Fire or Fire/Ground.

protect_ledger.payoff: real - blocked Incineroar's Fake Out and the Sandygast half of Excadrill's Rock Slide on turn one
real - blocked a 2x Rock Slide at 55/123, which was lethal
real - at 24/108 it blocked both a 2x Earthquake and an Air Slash, either of which would have KOed it

protect_note: Three Protects, all three with a genuine payoff, no consecutive-use failures and no empty guarding. Cadence is good.

ai_observations.note: Numel at 24/108 chose Earth Power into a Flying-type Togekiss on T4 ('It doesn't affect Togekiss...'), a completely dead move, when Heat Wave was available and would have hit both of my battlers. Recorded as an observation rather than a defect because the state shows it had just entered and Togekiss had also just switched in, so the Flying typing may not have been revealed to it at decision time; it did not repeat the mistake.

level_changes.reason: Brief rule 5: first optimized attempt won in five turns with ZERO player faints. Torkoal is the lowest member of the team by a wide margin - offset 0 against 2, 4 and 5 - and it is also the entire strategy: no Torkoal, no sun, and the other three members are just Fire types standing in ordinary weather. It is the one member on this team where a level directly buys the plan more turns, because Eruption's power scales with its remaining HP and it was flinched out of the strong one and then killed before the second.

Same trigger; Mawile is the second-lowest member at +2. It died to a single critical Earthquake without acting despite 130 HP and a Life Orb. I am less confident this one earns its level than Torkoal does - its real problem is a 2x Ground weakness on a team that already has two other Ground-weak members - so this is the smaller half of the bump and I would reverse it before I reversed Torkoal's if the retest shows the fight swinging too far. Deliberately not applied to Sandygast (+4) or Numel (+5), which are already well above the player cap.

cooler: The sun-grunt concept is right for Mt. Chimney and I would keep it - a Magma grunt on a volcano fielding Drought is exactly the kind of place-appropriate design the book asks for, and Simple Numel with Flame Charge is a much better idea than another Amnesia wall. My concrete observation is about where the levels sit rather than about the species. This team's offsets are inverted relative to how much each member matters: Numel is at +5 and Sandygast at +4, and neither of them is the plan, while Torkoal - which IS the plan, since it is the only source of sun and the only Eruption - sits at offset 0, two levels below the player cap, on a body that is 2x to Ground, 2x to Rock and 2x to Water. The result is that the sun engine is the most killable thing on the field, and in this battle it was flinched out of its best turn and then removed on turn three, after which the other three members were just Fire types in fading weather. If this fight is ever revisited beyond a level pass, the interesting question is how to make Torkoal survive to Erupt twice: a Shuca Berry or a partner that can absorb the obvious Ground answer would change the encounter far more than another level on Numel. Second, smaller note: three of the four members are weak to Ground, and one Earthquake user with a Flying partner beat the whole team without taking a KO. That shared hole is the real difficulty ceiling here, not the levels.
authored_set_legality: No legality problem found. Drought with Charcoal, Water Compaction with Eviolite, Simple with Eviolite and Intimidate with Life Orb were all live on the correct members. Magcargo-style invented abilities did not appear; Sandygast's Water Compaction is correctly the printed ability.
